title: Coherent generators and a morphism criterion for finite-cover sites
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention] whose category has finite limits and whose topology is generated by a pretopology consisting of finite covering families. Write $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ and $H_U=h_U^\#$ for the sheafification of the representable presheaf of an object $U$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Each $H_U$ is a coherent object in the sense of [def-trf-coherent-topos], and these objects form a generating family whose closure under finite limits in $\mathcal E$ consists of coherent objects. In particular $\mathcal E$ is a coherent topos. If $\mathcal E'$ is any coherent topos and $u:\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E$ is a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] such that $u^{-1}H_U$ is coherent for every $U\in\mathcal C$, then $u^{-1}$ takes every coherent object of $\mathcal E$ to a coherent object of $\mathcal E'$, so $u$ is coherent.

source.place: §8.1, printed p. 17: the finite-cover-site coherence criterion and preservation of coherent objects used for the triple sites. The same criterion is used in literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Exposé XI, proof of Lemma 2.5, printed pp. 178–179 (PDF pp. 184–185). This node states the abstract criterion, not its oriented-product application.

proof.text: Use the given finite-cover pretopology as the covering families of $\mathcal C$; sheaves for it are the sheaves of its generated topology by the stated sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Every covering family in this presentation is already finite, so condition (i) of [lem-trf-site-quasicompact-sheafification-criterion] holds with the identity refinement. Consequently every $H_U$ is quasi-compact. No subcanonical hypothesis is used.

proof.text: The adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies maps $H_U\to F$ with maps $h_U\to F$. Such a natural transformation is determined by $s\in F(U)$ and has component $f:V\to U\mapsto F(f)(s)$; evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_U$ is its inverse. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(H_U,F)\simeq F(U)$ without assuming $h_U$ is a sheaf. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], $H_1\simeq1$, $H_V\times H_W\simeq H_{V\times W}$, and $H_V\times_{H_U}H_W\simeq H_{V\times_U W}$ when the two maps come from arrows of $\mathcal C$: representable presheaves have these limits since their sections are the corresponding sets of compatible arrows.

proof.text: Take $E=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-covering-representable-coequalizer-presentation]; singleton identity coverings verify its covering hypothesis. Its coequalizer map $\coprod_jH_{U_j}\to F$ is epic by the displayed universal property: two maps out of $F$ equal after this map are the same coequalizer factorization. Hence the $H_U$ generate. If $F$ is quasi-compact, the definition [def-trf-coherent-topos] selects finitely many summands of this epimorphism. Therefore every quasi-compact $F$ has a finite jointly epimorphic family of maps from $H_U$. Smallness follows from the site and the containing universe.

source.place: Tags 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable), 0D06 (lemma-quasi-compact); agent expansion of the finite-cover coherence argument.

proof.text: We will use elementary quasi-compactness calculus. For any sheaf epimorphism $D\to F$, a local lift of a section of $F$ remains a lift in its pullback, because pullbacks are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]; [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] then proves pullback stability. Coproducts are sheafifications of objectwise disjoint unions: maps from that sheafification to a sheaf are exactly families of maps from the summands by the adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], a coproduct section locally belongs to one summand. Thus jointly epimorphic families remain jointly epimorphic after pullback. Pull a covering family of $F$ back to a quasi-compact $D$ and select finitely many members; their images cover $F$ if $D\to F$ is epic. This proves that epimorphic images of quasi-compact objects are quasi-compact. Similarly, pull a covering family of a finite coproduct back to each quasi-compact summand and take the union of the finitely many selected indices. A finite coproduct of quasi-compact objects is therefore quasi-compact, including the empty coproduct (its only subobject is itself, by strictness in [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity]).

source.place: Tags 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable), 0D06 (lemma-quasi-compact); agent expansion of the finite-cover coherence argument.

proof.text: Let $b:H_V\to H_U$ and $c:H_W\to H_U$ be arbitrary sheaf maps. Step 2 represents them by sections of $H_U(V)$ and $H_U(W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], there are finite coverings $(V_a\to V)_a$ and $(W_b\to W)_b$ on which these sections come from actual arrows $V_a\to U$ and $W_b\to U$. Coverings induce jointly epic maps $H_{V_a}\to H_V$: if two maps from $H_V$ to a sheaf agree on those objects, their corresponding sections agree by the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The same holds for $W$. Step 4 and pullback stability consequently give a finite jointly epic family onto $H_V\times_{H_U}H_W$ with members $H_{V_a}\times_{H_U}H_{W_b}\simeq H_{V_a\times_U W_b}$ (step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]). These members are quasi-compact by step 1; their finite coproduct and its epimorphic image are quasi-compact by step 4. This establishes the required quasi-compact pullbacks even when $b,c$ are not induced by global site arrows.

proof.text: For quasi-compact $B,C$ with maps to $H_U$, choose finite jointly epic families $H_{V_i}\to B$ and $H_{W_j}\to C$ by step 3. Pulling them back gives a finite jointly epic family $H_{V_i}\times_{H_U}H_{W_j}\to B\times_{H_U}C$. The members are quasi-compact by step 5, so step 4 proves that $B\times_{H_U}C$ is quasi-compact. This is precisely quasi-separatedness in [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Together with step 1 it makes every $H_U$, including $H_1\simeq1$, coherent.

source.place: Tags 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable), 0D06 (lemma-quasi-compact); agent expansion of the finite-cover coherence argument.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal D$ for the objects that are quasi-compact subobjects of some $H_U$. A subobject $T\hookrightarrow H_U$ is quasi-separated: for maps $B,C\to T$ their pullback is $B\times_{H_U}C$, since the inclusion is monic. Thus each member of $\mathcal D$ is coherent. It contains the $H_U$ and the terminal object. Because $1$ is quasi-separated, products of quasi-compact objects are quasi-compact. If $T\hookrightarrow H_U$ and $S\hookrightarrow H_V$ belong to $\mathcal D$, then $T\times S\hookrightarrow H_{U\times V}$ is a quasi-compact subobject, hence belongs to $\mathcal D$. For arbitrary arrows $f,g:T\rightrightarrows S$, $\operatorname{Eq}(f,g)=T\times_{S\times S}S$, with $S\to S\times S$ the diagonal. Here $S\times S$ lies in $\mathcal D$ and is quasi-separated, so the equalizer is quasi-compact and, being a subobject of $T\hookrightarrow H_U$, belongs to $\mathcal D$. This proves closure under finite products and equalizers, hence all finite limits. Starting with the small family $H_U$, close under these two finite constructions in successive stages, choosing one limit for each finite diagram; morphisms form sets in the containing universe [def-weil-size-convention], so the union is a small full generating subcategory of $\mathcal D$. All its objects are coherent. Therefore the closure under finite limits consists of coherent objects, and $\mathcal E$ is a coherent topos [def-trf-coherent-topos].

source.place: Tags 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable), 0D06 (lemma-quasi-compact); agent expansion of the finite-cover coherence argument.

proof.text: We also need finite coproducts of coherent objects to be coherent. Quasi-compactness was proved in step 4. For maps from quasi-compact $B,C$ to $\coprod_{i=1}^n A_i$ with each $A_i$ coherent, [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity] decomposes $B=\coprod_i B_i$ and $C=\coprod_i C_i$ into their pullbacks to the summands. Each $B_i$ is quasi-compact: extend any covering family of $B_i$ by the complementary summand $\coprod_{j\ne i}B_j$ to cover $B$, select finitely many members by quasi-compactness of $B$, and pull back to $B_i$; disjointness removes the complement. Likewise each $C_i$ is quasi-compact. The same extensivity statement gives $B\times_{\coprod A_i}C\simeq\coprod_i(B_i\times_{A_i}C_i)$. The summands are quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness of $A_i$, so the pullback is quasi-compact by step 4. This proves quasi-separatedness of the coproduct. The empty case is the strict initial object. These arguments work in any coherent topos: by [def-trf-coherent-topos] it is the category of sheaves of sets on a small site of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], to which step 4 and [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity] apply.

source.place: Tags 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable), 0D06 (lemma-quasi-compact); agent expansion of the finite-cover coherence argument.

proof.text: Let $A$ be an arbitrary coherent object of $\mathcal E$. Step 3 gives an epimorphism $p:P=\coprod_{i=1}^nH_{U_i}\to A$. Its kernel pair $R=P\times_A P$ is quasi-compact: $P$ is quasi-compact by step 4 and $A$ is quasi-separated. Apply step 3 again to obtain an epimorphism $Q=\coprod_{j=1}^mH_{V_j}\to R$. The finite integers $m,n$ can be zero. This explicitly constructs a finite presentation of the objects and relations; it does not assume $R$ is representable or that a subobject of a quasi-compact object must be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tags 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable), 0D06 (lemma-quasi-compact); agent expansion of the finite-cover coherence argument.

proof.text: Put $L=u^{-1}$. By [def-trf-geometric-morphism], $L$ is a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint. It preserves coproducts: $\operatorname{Hom}(L(\coprod_i T_i),Z)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(T_i,u_*Z)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(LT_i,Z)$. It preserves epimorphisms: under the adjunction, right cancellation after $Lp$ is right cancellation after $p$. Apply $L$ to both epimorphisms of step 9. By hypothesis all $LH_U$ are coherent, so $LP\simeq\coprod_iLH_{U_i}$ is coherent by step 8, while $LQ\simeq\coprod_jLH_{V_j}$ is quasi-compact. Its epimorphic image $LR$ is quasi-compact by step 4 applied to the small-site presentation of $\mathcal E\prime$ given by [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Finite-limit preservation identifies $LR\simeq LP\times_{LA}LP$ with the kernel pair of the epimorphism $Lp:LP\to LA$ (the projections are the images of those of $R$).

source.place: Tags 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable), 0D06 (lemma-quasi-compact); agent expansion of the finite-cover coherence argument.

proof.text: The coherent topos $\mathcal E\prime$, the coherent object $LP$, and the epimorphism $Lp:LP\to LA$ with quasi-compact kernel pair $LR$ now satisfy exactly [lem-trf-coherent-epimorphic-quotient]. Hence $LA$ is coherent. Since $A$ was an arbitrary coherent object, $u^{-1}$ preserves every coherent object, which is precisely that $u$ is coherent [def-trf-coherent-topos].
